text:
sofia: heads-up - after the gpu-operator 1.8.0 rollout in eu-west this morning a bunch of cuda-enabled nodes are showing as 'No GPUs' to the scheduler. noticed job failures and autoscaler not provisioning spare capacity.

sam: saw that too. logs show device-plugin registering different driver version than kernel module loaded. suspect the operator shipped a new driver installer path.

lee: exact kubelet log snippet i pulled: 
```
W0727 07:12:43.123456 1 deviceplugin.go:210] plugin for nvidia returned device list empty, reason: driver mismatch (cuda 12.1 vs kernel-module 510.6)
E0727 07:12:43.123789 1 kubelet_plugin.go:98] failed to advertise devices: found 0 usable GPUs
```

sofia: infra-bot flagged a capacity regression at 07:15 and cordoned 3 nodes automatically (eu-west-3a). infra-bot: any other automated actions?

infra-bot: auto-actions: cordon + notify on nodes with 0 GPUs and recent nvidia-driver change. created ticket INF-9543.

nina: quick mitigation suggestion - roll back gpu-operator to 1.7.2 and restart kubelet on affected nodes, that version still uses the old driver-installer path which matched our kernel modules.

sam: rolling back will help short-term but we need the root cause: why did kernel modules not match the driver? we haven't changed kernel versions. possible race in driver package install vs. module build on boot.

lee: observed this in the node kube-proxy init logs: 
```
+ installing nvidia-driver 540.2
+ dkms build nvidia-540.2 for kernel 5.10.0-202
ERROR: kernel headers not found for 5.10.0-202
```

sofia: that explains it. nodes that had rebooted during the operator rollout missed header packages (we had a late kernel-backport last week). operator assumed module build succeeded.

ops-manager: cost/priority note: eu-west cluster is heavily used for experiments — if we cordon too many nodes, cost goes up because traffic shifts to other regions and we spin reserved capacity. prefer targeted fixes.

nina: proposed immediate playbook:
- uncordon nodes that have matching driver/module (verify with `nvidia-smi`)
- on nodes with missing headers: install kernel-headers then trigger DKMS rebuild and `systemctl restart kubelet`
- temporarily set deployment nodeSelector for low-priority workloads to avoid the affected pool

sam: commands i used to patch one node: 
```
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y linux-headers-$(uname -r)
sudo dkms autoinstall
sudo modprobe nvidia
# verify
nvidia-smi
systemctl restart kubelet
```

lee: after doing that on 3 nodes, device-plugin advertised devices again and pending jobs started scheduling.

sofia: longer term actions:
- add a preflight check in our gpu-operator rollout that verifies kernel-headers + dkms build success before marking node ready
- add e2e job that reboots nodes post-driver install and confirms device plugin sees GPUs
- pin operator to specific driver-installer path until we have matrixed tests for kernel versions in eu-west

ops-manager: agree. also open action: tune cluster-autoscaler to prefer other AZs first to avoid immediate churn in eu-west if a rollback occurs.

infra-bot: ticket INF-9543 updated: label=infra, severity=high, assignees=sofia,sam,nina. rollback PR opened: #4123.

nina: one more wrinkle - some older jobs reported NCCL version mismatch in pod logs: 
```
NCCL WARN Call 0 failed: incompatibility between libnccl.so (2.12) and driver (2.10)
```
this suggests some containers still ship older NCCL libs; will coordinate with runtime-images team to ensure images use the distro's nccl symlink to system library.

sam: timeline: rolling back gpu-operator in eu-west completed at 07:40, restarted kubelets gradually, by 08:05 capacity returned to ~98%. keeping monitoring for regression windows.

sofia: thanks all — follow-ups: create preflight check repo issue, schedule operator canary on a small node-pool first, and coordinate runtime-images change with build team. i'll update INF-9543 with tasks. :white_check_mark:

lee: quick note: let's tag nodes with `gpu.operator.last_applied=1.8.0` when operator updates so we can query which nodes to prioritize for post-upgrade checks.

ops-manager: noted for runbook updates and cost impact tracking.

infra-bot: channel alert cleared at 08:20 — monitoring continues for 2h.
